doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: What Rollins wanted from his pianist; laying out
summary: Rollins liked simple chords and left solos to Soskin. Soskin talks about laying out when playing with Rich Perry.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did he tell you or suggest things about your playing that he wanted you to do or did he leave you to your own devices?

Okay what he liked was simple chords, not really substitute chords or anything like that. He just wanted the basic thing. And when I would solo, that was up to me. So when I played, it was just the basics. And we took it from there.
I wonder if you, when you’re backing him up or other horn players, do you ever lay out like on purpose?

Yeah. Well sometimes I mean tonight I’m playing with an amazing tenor saxophone player, Rich Perry. And you know we’re doing all my music. And so sometimes I’ll lay out but we’re doing my music so it’s got to be, you know, together.
Okay. Yeah you might want to be in — I’ll tell you the reason I asked that question. I very much enjoyed your recording on “Walk Tall.”
